text: Brown Norway rats with acute myeloid leukemia (induced by intraperitoneal injection of 10⁷ promyelocytic leukemia cells) were compared with healthy controls to test whether leukemia-associated oxidative stress evokes depression-like changes. Depression-like behavior was assessed via forced swim test at 30 or 34 days; spleen, cortex and hippocampus were excised. Leukemia altered locomotory and forced swim behavior in the 34-day series. Oxidative stress signs appeared at every stage: FRAP and glutathione were significantly lowered, while HO-1 mRNA and malondialdehyde were increased in spleen and brain. Glycine potency to displace [³H]L-689,560 from the NMDA receptor glycine site increased at 30 and 34 days; cortical 5-HT₂A receptors were upregulated at 30 days only. Conclusion: cortical antioxidant disturbances accompany NMDA glycine-site activation, characteristic of depression models, linking glutamatergic activity, oxidative stress and leukemia.
